messages:
IncidentBot: [SEV2] elevated error rate on /v1/generate (us-west-2) — 10.7% 5xx, started approx 2026-03-14 02:50 UTC. Paging: @Jordan L @Priya K. Alert: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/67890

Jordan L: I'm on it. Quick snapshot: LB reports upstream 502/504 spikes; some runtime pods are restarting. Priya do you have the runtime rotation?

Priya K: I'm primary for runtime until 07:00 UTC. Mira is secondary. I'll join now. What's the customer impact?

SupportOncall: multiple customer errors reported (3 new tickets, one live chat). Customers report `500` when calling generate with longer prompts ~>1500 tokens.

Mira Chen: runtime notes: we had a live model rollout (quantized-v3) in us-west-2 at 02:30 UTC. Telemetry shows increased tail latency for long sequences and occasional handler exits with `index out of range` in kv-cache code.

Alex P: infra-side, I've been paged too. Kevin, are nodes healthy? Any network flaps?

Kevin Ramos: nodes healthy; no OOMs. We did see higher retransmits in az-b for a 90s window at 02:48, but it recovered. LB logs show upstream read timeout to several pods.

SecurityOncall: quick glance at auth logs — no mass auth failures. I can keep watching but not the primary lead.

Jordan L: plan suggestion: roll back model variant to quantized-v2 in us-west-2 for traffic to stop hitting the problematic codepath, then keep quantized-v3 in canary elsewhere while runtime team investigates. Thoughts?

Priya K: rollback is safe and will restore service quickly. We'll need a deployment rollback in the runtime cluster and to force a cold start to clear any corrupted kv-cache entries.

Alex P: agree. Who's executing rollback? Priya you or infra? Also who's owning customer comms?

Kevin Ramos: infra can trigger the rollback if runtime agrees. We can run `kubectl set image` for the deployment to previous tag and do a gradual rollout to avoid capacity blips.

Priya K: runtime will own the rollback. I'm executing now: `kubectl -n runtime-prod set image deployment/runtime-gen-usw2 runtime=runtime:quantized-v2 && kubectl rollout status deployment/runtime-gen-usw2`

(2m later)

Priya K: rollback in progress — pods replacing. Monitoring logs to ensure no more `index out of range` panics.

Mira Chen: confirming logs show new pods started with quantized-v2 image. No panic stacktrace so far.

SupportOncall: posting customer update: "We're investigating elevated errors on generate in us-west-2 and rolling back a recent model rollout to restore service. Estimated recovery <20m. We'll update ASAP."

Jordan L: routing / runbook question while this is warm: should runtime be paged immediately for any 5xx on generate, or should infra be paged first when LB reports 502/504? Right now paging sometimes duplicates effort. We should codify.

Alex P: my take: if alerts contain runtime exception traces or pod restarts -> page runtime; if alerts indicate LB upstream timeouts with no pod restarts -> page infra; if both present or ambiguous -> page both. Also page support for customer comms and security if auth signals appear.

Kevin Ramos: propose adding a short escalation matrix to the oncall runbook and tagging which teams to route to based on top-level alert signals: `trace present / pod CRs / image rollout -> runtime`, `LB upstream timeouts / network flaps -> infra`, `auth errors -> security`, `tickets -> support`.

Priya K: I'll add the runtime snippet to the runbook (link: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/runtime-oncall) and include a rollback checklist and `kubectl` commands to expedite mitigation.

SecurityOncall: I'll add a quick note about when to page security (mass token failures, anomalous IPs, suspicious auth spikes) and include the basic queries.

Jordan L: small coverage gap surfaced — our duty roster for midnight-06:00 UTC currently has only one infra person in PST until 03:00, then a single EMEA person. That creates a blindspot if infra gets paged and is overloaded. We should propose overlapping infra coverage for critical windows.

Kevin Ramos: noted. I'll raise in next oncall rota sync. For now, infra can escalate to eng-sre if overloaded.

(After rollback completes)

Priya K: rollback complete. Error rate down from 10.7% -> 1.1% in 8 minutes. No further pod restarts.

SupportOncall: updating customers: "Service restored in us-west-2; we rolled back a recent model variant. We're following up with root cause and will issue a postmortem." :white_check_mark:

Jordan L: mitigation success. Next steps: runtime to open a bug for the kv-cache bounds check with failing prompt-length reproduction, add unit test, and avoid risky quantized-v3 rollout until fixed. Priya please own the bug and assign ETA.

Priya K: I'll file the issue and set ETA EOW for the fix + tests.

Alex P: handoff / shifts: I'm primary until 09:00 UTC. Priya you remain runtime primary; Mira secondary. Jordan you stay incident lead until we close the thread. Any gaps for the next handoff?

Mira Chen: I'll be available for 30m and then take the 06:00-14:00 UTC shift. No gaps on runtime.

Jordan L: routing action items recap: 1) add escalation matrix to runtime & infra runbooks, 2) add quick rollback checklist to runtime runbook, 3) infra to document LB->pod correlation checks, 4) security to add auth triage snippet, 5) ops to review rota for overlap. Who will own doc updates?

Priya K: runtime doc = me.

Kevin Ramos: infra doc = me.

SecurityOncall: security doc = me.

SupportOncall: I'll post a short customer-facing summary and link to postmortem when ready.

IncidentBot: Incident 2026-03-14-67890 status changed to MITIGATED by Jordan L. Postmortem due in 2 business days.

Jordan L: thanks all. Handoff reminder: I'm incident lead until 03:30 UTC; Alex remains primary until 09:00 UTC. Priya/Mira keep an eye for regression for 60m. Good work.

Alex P: great work everyone. Filing the initial incident note to central tracker.

Priya K: acknowledged, monitoring for 60m then will close watches.

SupportOncall: tickets updated and customers notified. Closing live chat.

Mira Chen: will do a quick post-mortem blameless summary and link it in the runbook updates.

Jordan L: closing thread for now, will re-open if error rate >2% for 10m.

(End of thread)
